findings.issue: The 'Admin-ping aggregator' design (AC at lines 37-46) introduces a structured, code-grouped, per-source aggregator with 7 explicit error codes (FEED_HTTP_<status>, FEED_TIMEOUT, FEED_XML_PARSE, ART_FALLBACK_HTTP_<status>, ART_FALLBACK_TIMEOUT, ART_FALLBACK_PARSE_EMPTY, ART_PARSE_EXCEPTION) and a custom message template '[<INSTANCE_LABEL>] orangetrack: N issues this tick — • <CODE> (<count>×) — <link>' for a failure surface that fires at most ~1 fetch/day. This is a brand-new admin-ping subsystem that does not exist for any of the three current sources. Today every source either piggybacks on the generic catch-all in news_bot.py:1471 ('⚠️ Source {fetcher_name} failed: {safe}') or relies on the per-parser notifier= callback (lamley/mattel) emitting a single ad-hoc string. There is no precedent for an in-tick aggregator, error-code taxonomy, or instance-label-prefixed bullet list, and the tech-spec will inherit a design that is materially heavier than the three existing parsers combined.
findings.why_matters: The codebase is in observation mode with an explicit 'additive, low-risk' constraint. Introducing a structured error-code taxonomy + grouping logic for a feature whose entire admin-ping volume is bounded by 1 fetch/day x ~1 fallback HTTP/article (rare) inverts the cost/benefit balance: the code that aggregates and groups will be larger and more complex than the parser it instruments. It also creates a single-source-of-its-kind pattern — when a fifth source is added, either (a) every source gets retrofitted to the new template (large additive change), or (b) the channel grows two ping styles. Both outcomes are worse than reusing the existing single-string notifier that lamley/mattel already use successfully. This is precisely the over-engineering the molyanov-default-with-pushback memory targets.
findings.fix: Drop the aggregator. Reuse the existing pattern: parser raises → news_bot's outer try/except (news_bot.py:1467-1476) emits one '⚠️ Source orangetrack failed: <sanitized>' line; the per-article fallback exceptions can use the same notifier= callback the lamley parser already uses. If the operator genuinely needs codes for grepping journalctl, log the codes inside the parser at WARNING/ERROR level (free, no admin-ping touch) and keep the channel-level admin pings as terse single strings. Save 'aggregated structured admin pings' for a separate cross-source observability feature when there's actual evidence three sources are noisy.

findings.issue: Throttle + 429 Retry-After handling (AC line 54) for a path that fires at most twice in one tick. AC says 'при двух подряд fallback-HTTP-запросах в один cron-tick (редкий случай) второй запрос ждёт MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL_S секунд (lamley-паттерн); 429 с заголовком Retry-After уважается один раз.' The fallback HTTP only fires when content:encoded is empty, which the spec itself describes as 'срабатывает редко' (line 22). With cron at 1 fetch/day and ~1 article/day, the realistic 'two consecutive fallback HTTP in one tick' rate is essentially zero.
findings.why_matters: Carrying lamley's throttle/WAF/Retry-After plumbing into a parser that has none of lamley's hostile-host conditions (orangetrack is plain WordPress.com, no Cloudflare per AC line 60 and code-research §3) is YAGNI. It also adds test surface (must mock time.sleep, must mock 429 response, must reset throttle state between tests) for a code path that real traffic will never exercise.
findings.fix: Remove the throttle and Retry-After clauses. If the operator one day sees a 429 from WordPress.com, that's a one-line addition. The spec already self-marks the case as 'редкий случай' — the right answer for a rare case is 'log it and move on,' not 'implement a state machine.'

findings.issue: User-spec contains tech-spec-grade implementation detail. AC line 47 specifies a regex literal ('^quick link[!:].*\b(buy|order|grab|shop)\b/i'), AC line 53 prescribes the parser walking strategy ('DOM walking strategy: парсер ходит по HTML-тегам, а не по Gutenberg-классам'), AC line 54 names a constant (MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL_S), AC line 55 references a specific cache window size ('окно из 10-20 свежих записей'), AC line 52 names file paths and FILES list line ranges, and the 'Технические решения' section reads like a tech-spec rationale doc. This is HOW, not WHAT/WHY.
findings.why_matters: User-spec is supposed to define WHAT (criteria) and WHY (motivation). When implementation-level decisions land in user-spec acceptance criteria, the tech-spec stage loses its degrees of freedom — the implementer cannot, for example, choose a different regex or use a class-based selector even if the BeautifulSoup signature changes. It also pollutes the operator-readable spec with details a non-programmer cannot review.
findings.fix: Move the regex literal, MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL_S name, FILES-list line ranges, DOM-walking strategy, and 'окно 10-20 записей' rationale to tech-spec.md. Replace user-spec ACs with operator-meaningful outcomes: 'Standalone affiliate paragraphs (e.g. "QUICK LINK! Buy ... now.") are filtered before LLM translation,' 'Parser still works after a WordPress theme change that drops wp-block-* classes (validated by test).' Keep 'Технические решения' brief — operator-facing rationale only.

findings.issue: Size 'M' is undersold. The spec covers: (1) a new parser module (~150-200 LoC per code-research §3), (2) boilerplate filter pattern + tests (3-5 cases per AC), (3) NETLOC_TO_SOURCE + SOURCE_EMOJI + SOURCE_LABEL + fetch_full_article dispatcher edits in news_bot.py, (4) feeds.json edit, (5) deploy.sh + deploy.yml mirror invariant edit, (6) tests/test_orangetrack_source.py (~150-200 LoC, 8-12 cases per code-research §7, but spec promises ~30-40 tests), (7) tests/test_sources_registry.py set-assertion update, (8) the proposed admin-ping aggregator (with its own 7-code state, message template, instance label, dedup logic, plus tests for each code), (9) throttle + Retry-After plumbing + tests. After dropping the aggregator and throttle (per other findings), the residual scope is genuinely M-sized. With them in, this is L: ~30-40 new tests is itself an L signal — no other source has that many.
findings.why_matters: Mis-sized features blow through the molyanov-default budget and then get retrofitted. If the M label is preserved, the agent will commit to an M-sized tech-spec pass and discover the aggregator's edge cases (instance-label, code grouping, link dedup, FEED_* vs ART_* rollup) under time pressure.
findings.fix: Either (a) demote scope per the overengineering findings, keep size M; or (b) keep scope, relabel size L and split into two iterations: iteration 1 = parser + boilerplate + registry edits + tests + deploy-list mirror, iteration 2 = the per-source admin-ping aggregator (which then could be designed cross-source rather than orangetrack-only). Option (a) is strongly preferred.

findings.issue: RSS-recovery via natural feed window (AC line 55, R5 line 75) is adequate as designed BUT the user-visible behavior on the rare loss case is undocumented. The spec says 'Если случится — оператор может вручную скачать пропущенные через архивный hw_review путь' but does not state how the operator detects the loss in the first place. There is no acceptance criterion for 'operator is notified when feed becomes stale beyond N days' or 'fetched_at vs pubDate gap exceeds threshold.'
findings.why_matters: Observation-mode operator is non-programmer; the bot silently dropping 1-3 weeks of orangetrack content because the site was down would be invisible. This is a small gap, not a critical one — R5 itself estimates probability near zero — but documenting the detection-and-recovery flow (even as 'no detection, accept loss') protects the operator from confusion later.
findings.fix: Add one-line acceptance: either 'No staleness detection in this feature; operator accepts that >7-day outage of the source coupled with >10 missed posts may cause permanent loss (R5)' OR 'Stale-feed warning if last successful orangetrack fetch produced new entries >7 days ago.' The first option is fine — just make the silence explicit.

findings.issue: AC line 50 promises '740 baseline + ~30-40 new tests'. The architecture.md states the suite is '~500 tests after llm-transcreation feature' — there is a mismatch of ~240 tests between the two numbers, and the spec's 'Как проверить' table likewise asserts 740. One of these counts is stale.
findings.why_matters: Test-count assertions in acceptance criteria become regression-style gates: if the implementer runs pytest and gets 510 vs 540, the AC may be marked failed without a real defect. The number itself isn't load-bearing for the feature, but the ambiguity is.
findings.fix: Remove the absolute baseline number. Replace with 'Все существующие тесты остаются зелёными; добавлено N новых' — N can stay if you want a soft target, but '740 baseline' should be checked against actual `pytest --collect-only | tail -1` and reconciled (likely should be ~500-540 per architecture.md, plus whatever was added since).

findings.issue: The hybrid feed-first + HTML-fallback architecture (Decision 1, AC line 22, R1) is justified BUT the code-research explicitly recommends a feed-only design: 'Architecture = FEED-ONLY parser (no article-page scrape). RSS content:encoded already carries the full HTML body' (code-research line 5). Code-research §3 documents that orangetrack's content:encoded is the FULL body in the live capture, not a lamley-style excerpt, and §1 recommends 'Pure-parse, no HTTP — the entry already has the full body inline.' The user-spec adopts a feed-first + fallback shape anyway, justified as 'defensive fallback (срабатывает редко).' But the empirical evidence in code-research suggests the fallback path is dead code that adds: (a) HTTP plumbing, (b) throttle plumbing per the other finding, (c) admin-ping codes ART_FALLBACK_*, (d) Retry-After handling, (e) ~6-8 extra tests. All for a path the live-feed sample never exercises.
findings.why_matters: If content:encoded is empty in some future post, the most likely cause is a draft or a broken edit — re-fetching the article page won't necessarily recover content. Meanwhile every line of fallback code is permanent maintenance burden. The spec already concedes the path is 'defensive' and 'редкий случай' — that's exactly the YAGNI threshold.
findings.fix: Consider feed-only (per code-research recommendation): if entry.content[0].value is empty, return None (skip article) and emit a single admin-ping line. If a year of operation shows 0 occurrences, the decision validates itself. If a few empty content:encoded posts appear, escalate to the fallback in a separate small feature with real evidence. At minimum: justify in 'Технические решения' why you're overriding the code-research recommendation, or remove the fallback path.

summary: Spec is feasible and aligned with project conventions in its core (parser contract, blocks-path, deploy-list mirror invariant, source registry edits) but materially over-engineered around the admin-ping aggregator (custom 7-code taxonomy + grouping for a ~1/day failure surface) and the HTTP-fallback path's accompanying throttle/Retry-After plumbing (code-research recommends feed-only). Drop these, demote implementation details into tech-spec, and the M sizing and observation-mode discipline both hold.
